text: Mac Cécht was a minor Irish god. He was a farmer and the husband of Fódla, one of the goddesses of the land, a member of the magical race called the Tuatha Dé Danann. Fódla's name means divided or plowed land. His parallel name means plowman or son of the plow, so both were deities of agriculture. He may also have been a god of healing. When the king of the Tuatha Dé lay dying, Mac Cécht walked the parched land for water to revive him. A wild duck led him to a spring, and the Celts saw water as a source of healing. He was the son of Ogma, god of eloquent speech. He lost his life in combat with the invading Milesians. Another Mac Cécht championed the doomed king Conaire at Da Derga's hostel, killed the man who decapitated Conaire, and offered the king's head its last drink.
